sections.title: The letter name
paragraphs: The letter (I) /iː/ is called (I) /iː/. Its most common sound is the sound /ɪ/, heard in the word (Insel) /ˈɪnzl̩/, which means island. This letter makes three different sounds in German speech.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: For the first sound, open your mouth slightly and keep your tongue high. For the second sound, spread your lips wide and push your tongue higher forward. For the third sound, raise the middle of your tongue close to your roof. You can feel your vocal cords vibrate through every sound.

sections.title: Reading this letter
paragraphs: In closed syllables before two or more consonants, it sounds like the sound /ɪ/ in (bitte) /ˈbɪtə/. In open stressed syllables, it makes the long sound /iː/ in (Tiger) /ˈtiːɡɐ/. Before another vowel in borrowed words, it sounds like the sound /j/ in (Nation) /naˈtsi̯oːn/.

sections.title: Tips for English speakers
paragraphs: Do not turn the long vowel into a glide like the sound in see. Keep your tongue steady and your lips tense until the sound finishes. Do not drop the short vowel into a relaxed sound like the vowel in bit. Keep your tongue slightly higher and tighter.
